prompt.brief: Design Facebook's Like feature so a user can like or unlike a post, see an accurate-enough count, and receive live updates when other people interact with the same post.
successSignals: Separate the user's membership state from the denormalized count and define which result must be strongly consistent.
Make like and unlike idempotent, authorize the actor, and prevent duplicate state transitions under retries.
Use an ordered event stream and coalesced fan-out for live count updates without turning every viewer into a database reader.
Handle hot posts, celebrity traffic, reconnects, moderation deletes, and delayed or duplicated events explicitly.

functional: Allow an authenticated user to like or unlike a post and see whether they have liked it.
Display a count and optionally a preview of representative users who liked the post.
Push count and membership changes to viewers who are currently looking at the post.
Keep moderation, privacy, blocked-user, and deleted-post rules reflected in reads and events.
nonFunctional: The actor's own like state is read-after-write consistent; the aggregate count may be briefly eventually consistent.
Target p95 under 150 ms for a like write acknowledgement and under 2 seconds for a live count update.
Do not lose an accepted like or unlike; retries and duplicate deliveries must not create duplicate state.
A fan-out or analytics outage must not block the write path or expose private interactions.
scaleAssumptions: 1 billion registered users, 300 million daily active users, and 100 million posts receiving interactions each day.
Assume 20 million like/unlike operations per day on average, with 10x bursts during live events.
Most posts have fewer than 1,000 active viewers, but the hottest 1,000 posts can each have 100,000 viewers.
Retain the durable interaction ledger for product and moderation needs; aggregate counts are rebuilt from it when required.

metrics.label: Peak write rate
metrics.description: 20M daily mutations with a 10x burst; provision partitions and queues for more than the average.

metrics.label: Write acknowledgement
metrics.description: The user sees their own state after the conditional interaction write commits.

metrics.label: Live freshness
metrics.description: Coalesce count changes while exposing the last sequence and an offline/stale state.

metrics.label: Hot-post fan-out
metrics.description: Shard the subscriber set and send snapshots or deltas with backpressure.

entities.name: Post
entities.notes: The interaction service checks that the post exists and that the actor can view it before mutating state.

entities.name: Like
entities.notes: Use (post_id, user_id) as the uniqueness key; a tombstone or version prevents an old retry from resurrecting a like.

entities.name: LikeAggregate
entities.notes: A denormalized projection optimized for reads; it is corrected by replay or reconciliation rather than being the only source of truth.

entities.name: LikeEvent
entities.notes: An immutable, partitioned event carries the transition to projection, notifications, analytics, and repair consumers.

apis.notes: Authenticate and authorize the user; conditionally insert the unique interaction and return the committed projection or a safe read of it.
Make the delete idempotent and versioned; a repeated request returns the same logical state.
Read the user's state from the interaction store and the count from the aggregate cache with privacy filtering.
Authorize room membership, resume from last version when possible, and send a snapshot after a gap or reconnect.

dataFlow.title: Validate the interaction
dataFlow.description: The client sends a request ID. The edge and interaction service authenticate the actor, check post visibility and moderation state, and route by post_id.

dataFlow.title: Commit the user's like state
dataFlow.description: A conditional write keyed by (post_id, user_id) applies the requested state and request version. Replays return the existing result instead of creating a second like.

dataFlow.title: Publish the durable transition
dataFlow.description: After the interaction commit, an outbox or transactionally coupled change stream emits one LikeEvent. The acknowledgement does not wait for fan-out or analytics.

dataFlow.title: Update the aggregate projection
dataFlow.description: A partition owner consumes events in order, increments or decrements the post count idempotently, and publishes a monotonic version to the live update stream.

dataFlow.title: Broadcast asynchronously
dataFlow.description: The room service coalesces rapid changes and sends the newest count to subscribed viewers. Slow or reconnecting clients receive a fresh snapshot rather than every intermediate delta.

architecture.title: Facebook-like live likes reference architecture
architecture.summary: A durable interaction ledger is the source of truth for a user's like state; a versioned aggregate and coalesced live stream make counts fast without weakening write correctness.

layers.label: Experience layer
layers.description: Clients render the actor's state, aggregate count, and freshness-aware live updates.

layers.label: Interaction and projection layer
layers.description: The ledger commits idempotent state while a stream projects counts and distributes changes.

layers.label: Delivery and operations
layers.description: Hot-post fan-out, cache reads, repair, moderation, and analytics remain independently scalable.

keyPaths.label: Like write path
keyPaths.description: Client -> edge -> like service -> interaction ledger -> event stream.

keyPaths.label: Live update path
keyPaths.description: Event stream -> counter projector -> room service -> subscribed clients.

components.label: Post viewers
components.description: Render liked state and count; subscribe to the post room and reconnect with the last seen version.

components.label: Edge gateway
components.description: Terminates TLS, authenticates users, applies quotas, and routes requests by post key.

components.label: Like service
components.description: Checks visibility and moderation rules, applies idempotent like/unlike mutations, and returns committed state.

components.label: Interaction ledger
components.description: Durable source of truth keyed by post_id and user_id, with versions and tombstones for safe retries.

components.label: Change outbox
components.description: Makes committed state transitions observable to consumers even when the stream is temporarily unavailable.

components.label: Like event stream
components.description: Partitions events by post_id so each post's transitions can be ordered and replayed.

components.label: Count projector
components.description: Consumes idempotently, maintains versioned aggregates, and emits count changes for delivery.

components.label: Live room service
components.description: Tracks subscribers, shards hot rooms, coalesces updates, and applies backpressure to slow clients.

components.label: Room membership
components.description: Short-lived subscriber and shard state; loss causes reconnects, not loss of likes.

components.label: Count cache
components.description: Serves bounded-staleness count snapshots and absorbs read spikes for popular posts.

components.label: Analytics and moderation
components.description: Consumes sampled or full events for trends, abuse detection, audit, and offline repair.

components.label: Observability
components.description: Tracks mutation latency, stream lag, projection drift, fan-out drops, and hot-key pressure.

connections.label: Like / read
connections.description: Authenticated HTTPS requests and bounded snapshot reads.

connections.label: Authorized request
connections.description: Routes by post and enforces quotas before application logic.

connections.label: Conditional state
connections.description: Unique actor-post mutation with request idempotency.

connections.label: Committed transition
connections.description: Outbox/change stream preserves accepted mutations for consumers.

connections.label: LikeEvent
connections.description: At-least-once event delivery partitioned by post_id.

connections.label: Ordered events
connections.description: Projector deduplicates event IDs and advances post versions.

connections.label: Count snapshot
connections.description: Publishes the versioned aggregate for fast reads.

connections.label: Count update
connections.description: Sends coalescible changes to the live delivery tier.

connections.label: Room leases
connections.description: Short-lived membership state and hot-room shard assignments.

connections.label: Live count
connections.description: Pushes newest count and version over SSE or WebSocket.

connections.label: Snapshot read
connections.description: The client can render a stale-marked count when live delivery is unavailable.

connections.label: Async events
connections.description: Analytics and abuse detection do not block user acknowledgement.

connections.label: Lag and drift
connections.description: Observability detects consumer lag, hot partitions, and projection divergence.

deepDives.title: Strong user state versus approximate aggregate
points: The interaction ledger answers whether this user liked the post and is the correctness boundary for retries, moderation, and audit.
The count is a projection that can lag or be rebuilt; return version and observedAt so the UI does not imply false precision.
A read-after-write response can combine the mutation result with the latest known aggregate, while a reconciliation job repairs missed projections.

deepDives.title: Hot posts and fan-out
points: Partition the ledger and event stream by post, then split an exceptionally hot room across delivery shards.
Coalesce updates over a short window and drop intermediate deltas for slow clients; a client can always recover with a versioned snapshot.
Use admission limits and backpressure so one celebrity post cannot exhaust connection, broker, or egress capacity for other rooms.

deepDives.title: Idempotency, ordering, and recovery
points: A client request ID protects the write API; event IDs and per-post versions protect at-least-once consumers.
An unlike must not be overwritten by a late like retry, so compare versions or operation timestamps at the interaction key.
Replay the event stream into a new aggregate and compare it with the serving projection before repairing drift.

deepDives.title: Privacy, moderation, and deletion
points: Authorize room subscription and filter preview users; never infer visibility from the public count alone.
A moderated or deleted post stops new mutations and emits a tombstone that invalidates cache, room, and preview data.
Keep audit retention and user deletion semantics explicit; analytics copies need their own deletion or anonymization workflow.

tradeoffs.title: Exact count versus scalable count
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use a durable per-user ledger plus an eventually consistent versioned aggregate; make the freshness contract visible.
tradeoffs.caution: An exact read of every liker is too expensive for hot posts, while an unmarked approximate count can mislead users and reviewers.

tradeoffs.title: WebSocket versus SSE
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use SSE for one-way count updates and WebSocket when the product already needs bidirectional presence or reactions.
tradeoffs.caution: Either protocol still needs reconnect, authorization refresh, room sharding, and snapshot recovery; transport choice does not solve fan-out.

tradeoffs.title: Counter increments versus event replay
tradeoffs.recommendation: Apply idempotent increments for the serving path and retain events for replay, reconciliation, and new projections.
tradeoffs.caution: A counter-only design is fast but cannot recover confidently from dropped or duplicated messages.

commonMistakes: Treating the aggregate count as the source of truth for whether a user liked a post.
Writing one durable analytics row for every page viewer or live update.
Ignoring hot-key fan-out and assuming one process can broadcast to every viewer.
Using a simple toggle endpoint that is unsafe under retries and concurrent tabs.
Forgetting privacy, moderation, deleted posts, or stale-count labeling.

followUps.question: How would you show the first 100 people who liked a post?
followUps.answer: Maintain a privacy-filtered, bounded preview projection keyed by post and cursor, backed by the interaction ledger; never scan the full liker set on each post read.

followUps.question: What changes if the product requires an exact count?
followUps.answer: Keep the same ledger but make the count read from a strongly consistent aggregate or a transactionally maintained sharded counter, accepting higher write coordination and hot-key complexity.

followUps.question: How do you support offline mobile likes?
followUps.answer: Assign client operation IDs and versions, accept queued operations when authorized, resolve conflicts with a documented last-write or server-version rule, and reconcile the local UI from the committed response.

followUps.question: How do you detect a broken count projector?
followUps.answer: Compare sampled ledger counts with projections, alert on event lag and version gaps, and rebuild a shadow projection from the retained stream before switching or repairing it.

rubric.description: The answer distinguishes per-user like state from the count and makes retries, concurrency, and event duplication safe.
The design accounts for hot posts, partitioning, coalescing, subscriber sharding, cache reads, and burst capacity.
The response defines acknowledgement and live-update targets and exposes versions or stale state to clients.
Accepted writes survive downstream outages, while replay, reconciliation, and reconnect snapshots recover projections and clients.
Authentication, authorization, privacy, moderation, deletion, quotas, and observability are part of the design rather than afterthoughts.
